# Sirach Chapter 28 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 28 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**28:1** Take revenge on someone and you'll get revenge back from the LORD — God keeps a careful record of your sins.

**28:2** Forgive your neighbor for what they did to you, and then when you pray, your sins will be forgiven too.

**28:3** Can a person nurse a grudge against another person — and then turn around and ask the LORD to heal them?

**28:4** Won't show the slightest mercy to someone just like themselves — but wants God to overlook their own sins?

**28:5** They're flesh and blood, and they're holding onto their rage — who exactly is going to make things right for them?

**28:6** Think about the end: death, corruption — and stop hating. Remember where you're going and keep the commandments.

**28:7** Keep the commandments in mind; don't be angry with your neighbor. Remember the covenant of the Most High and let the offense go.

**28:8** Stay out of fights and you'll sin less; a hot-headed person is like bellows for a fire —

**28:9** and the sinner stirs up trouble among friends and throws quarrels like grenades among people who were living in peace.

**28:10** The bigger the pile of wood, the bigger the fire; the more stubborn the person, the bigger the fight; and the stronger they are, the hotter the anger burns.

**28:11** A quarrel rushed into lights a fire; a hasty dispute draws blood.

**28:12** Blow on a coal and it blazes; spit on it and it goes out — but both come from your mouth.

**28:13** Put a curse on the gossip and the two-faced liar, for they've destroyed many peaceful people.

**28:14** The meddling tongue has sent shock waves through communities, scattered people from nation to nation, demolished fortified cities, brought down the households of the powerful.

**28:15** The meddling tongue has driven capable wives from their homes and robbed them of everything they worked for.

**28:16** Whoever gets caught up in listening to it will never find rest; there's no peaceful life in it.

**28:17** A whip leaves a welt, but the tongue breaks bones.

**28:18** More people have been destroyed by the tongue than have ever died by the sword.

**28:19** Blessed is the person who's been shielded from it — who's never felt its fury, never had to drag its iron yoke or wear its chains.

**28:20** Because its yoke is iron and its chains are bronze.

**28:21** The death it deals is a horrible death; better to go to Hades than to suffer it.

**28:22** It has no power over those who fear God; the fire of it won't touch them.

**28:23** But those who have abandoned the LORD will fall right into it; in them it will burn without stopping. It will be sent against them like a roaring lion and tear them apart like a leopard.

**28:24** Fence your property in with thorns; lock down your silver and your gold.

**28:25** Then do the same for your mouth — put a door and a bolt on it; put your words on a scale and weigh them out.

**28:26** Watch yourself — don't slip through your words and fall into the trap of someone waiting for you.
